assumptions: Customer impact is taken to begin at 13:31 UTC, when the first division-by-zero errors appear in the logs, rather than at 13:36 UTC when the alert fired. The alert's own duration therefore understates how long customers were affected.
Recovery is asserted on the basis of the mitigation step reporting a return to baseline; the log excerpt available ends at 13:36 and contains no post-mitigation minutes to verify this independently.

The low-level errors seen before 13:31 (upstream payment-authorization timeouts, roughly 0-4% per minute) are treated as pre-existing background noise unrelated to this incident. They were not investigated.

At 13:31 the flag was evaluated as off for 21 and on for 179 of 200 evaluations, and fully on thereafter. This is read as a fast ramp rather than a partial rollout that stalled; the rollout mechanism and its configuration were not examined.
Who toggled the flag, and whether the toggle was intentional or part of a scheduled rollout, is not recorded in the evidence available.

The specific input condition that produces the zero divisor (which accounts, and why) was not determined; the fix was to disable the path, not to diagnose it. The underlying defect remains in the codebase behind the disabled flag.

The alternative explanation — an unrecorded deploy at 13:31 that both enabled the path and introduced the defect — was considered and judged unsupported by the absence of any deploy in the change log, but it was never actively ruled out.
input.executive_summary: On 12 September 2026, a new spending-summary capability was switched on for the online shop at 13:31 UTC. The new code failed whenever it tried to render a customer's account page for certain accounts, so those customers saw an error instead of their account page. Checkout and browsing were not implicated; the failures were confined to account pages. Automated monitoring raised an alert at 13:36 UTC, an automated investigation identified the newly enabled capability as the cause within about forty seconds, and the capability was switched back off at 13:37 UTC, after which the shop returned to its normal error levels. Customers were affected for roughly six minutes in total — about five minutes before the alert fired, and about one minute after. No data was lost or corrupted, and no customer action is required; affected customers would have succeeded on a retry after the fix.
input.root_cause: The `monthly-spend-feature` flag on io-shop was turned on at 13:31 UTC, routing account-page renders through a previously dormant code path that raises `ZeroDivisionError` (division by zero) for a large share of accounts. The flag toggle alone was sufficient to trigger it — the change log shows no deployment in the preceding 24 hours — and turning the flag back off at 13:37 returned the service to baseline.
